title: About US Quakes
intro: This map is not an earthquake or tsunami warning service. This copy is only as new as its last refresh, shown on the Live sheet. It draws the U.S. Geological Survey’s catalog of earthquakes in four map boxes: the Lower 48, Alaska with the Aleutians, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico with the Virgin Islands. {history} earthquakes from {firstYear} to {lastYear} ship with the app; the last {liveDays} days arrive with each refresh.

reading.title: Size
reading.text: Each whole step of magnitude doubles a dot’s area, down to magnitude {sizeFloor}; smaller earthquakes share the smallest dot. It is a display rule, not a measure of energy.

reading.title: Color
reading.text: Color is depth as the catalog gives it: straw near the surface, then amber, rose, mauve and violet, to slate navy at {rampDeepKm} km and deeper. The stops sit at {rampStops} km.

reading.title: Hollow
reading.text: A hollow ring is an automatic solution from the last {liveDays} days that no person has reviewed yet; it may move, change size or disappear. A ring is never drawn smaller than a magnitude {hollowMinMag} dot, so that its hole shows. Older rows the catalog still lists as automatic are drawn solid, and their card says so.

reading.title: Gray
reading.text: A gray dot has no depth in the catalog: {noDepth} rows in the history, {noDepthBefore1900} of them before {eraYear}.
A small × has no magnitude: {noMagnitude} rows, every one before {eraYear}. They are drawn only while the window reaches back before {eraYear}.

reading.title: Fade
reading.text: Within a window, older dots are paler; in All, every dot is drawn at the same half strength. The paleness is a display choice, not a measurement.

reading.title: Display choices
reading.text: These are presentation, not data: the color ramp and its stops; the thin rim around each dot, dark above {rimKm} km and light from {rimKm} km down; the fading of older dots; the faint trace Play leaves; the dimming outside a cross-section; the shaded relief, its level stretch and its strength; the tints of the sea; the hatching where the map ends; and the ink of the record strip, whose density counts events.

notes.title: Not a warning service
notes.text: This map is not an earthquake or tsunami warning service. This copy is only as new as its last refresh, shown on the Live sheet.

notes.title: More dots mostly means more seismometers
notes.text: The history holds {pre1950} earthquakes before {midYear} and {post2000} from {recentYear} on. Most of that rise is in the instruments, not in the Earth.

notes.title: What the catalog catches
notes.text: From {eraYear} this app keeps magnitude {floor} and up; before {eraYear}, every earthquake the catalog lists. Smaller earthquakes are missing unevenly from place to place.

notes.title: Magnitude types differ
notes.text: Each event’s card shows the magnitude type the catalog gives ({magTypeCount} labels in the history), and none is converted into another.

notes.title: Automatic solutions change or vanish
notes.text: A live earthquake marked automatic has not been checked by a person yet. Its place, depth or size may change, and it may be deleted.

notes.title: A depth of 10 km is often assigned
notes.text: {depth10km} earthquakes in the history sit at exactly {fixedDepthKm} km. That depth can be one assigned when the data could not fix one, and such rows line up flat in a cross-section.

notes.title: Negative depths
notes.text: {negDepth} rows in the history have a negative depth. The map colors them as {zeroKm} km deep, and the cross-section plots them above its {zeroKm} km line.

notes.title: Mercator inflates the north
notes.text: At {latN}° N a kilometer is drawn {ratioLen} times as long as at {latS}° N, so an area there looks {ratioArea} times as large. The scale bar is measured at the latitude of the map’s center.

notes.title: Boxes, not borders
notes.text: The four map boxes also take in earthquakes outside the United States, among them in {countries}, and the app shows them as they are. Counts are labeled by map box, never by state or country.

notes.title: Before 1900, nominal
notes.text: The catalog lists {before1900} earthquakes from {firstYear} to {lastPreYear}, {noDepthBefore1900} of them without a depth. Their times and positions are as the catalog lists them, often round numbers; the {cascadiaYear} Cascadia earthquake is a single point.

notes.title: The history is a snapshot
notes.text: Rows are as USGS listed them when retrieved on {retrieved}. Later revisions arrive only with a new copy of the app.

notes.title: Only earthquakes
notes.text: {droppedOther} other events in the catalog are left out, among them {nuclear} nuclear explosions, {quarry} quarry blasts and {explosions} explosions.

notes.title: Faults are not a hazard map
notes.text: The fault lines are the Quaternary Fault and Fold Database: evidence of movement in the geological past, not a rating of danger. Nearness is not cause: a dot beside a fault does not say that fault moved.

notes.title: Not monitored is not Normal
notes.text: A volcano the USGS does not list as monitored has no alert level. The map draws it empty and calls it not monitored, never Normal.

notes.title: Shaded relief
notes.text: Relief is drawn wherever the 3DEP elevation service had data: the United States and, near its borders, parts of Canada and Mexico; the Bahamas have none. The shading, its level stretch and its strength are display choices.

notShown.title: What this app does not show, and why
notShown.text: No globe and no worldwide catalog: the story here is the United States. No hazard model: a model is not a measurement. No ShakeMap or Did You Feel It? maps: they are separate USGS products; the felt count is shown. No Guam, Northern Marianas or American Samoa: they are outside the four map boxes. No explosions, quarry blasts or nuclear tests: they are not earthquakes. No heat maps, clustering or interpolated rates: each would draw something the catalog does not hold. No links: the app has no network.

mww.name: moment, W-phase
mww.quote: Derived from a centroid moment tensor inversion of the W-phase

mwc.name: moment, centroid
mwc.quote: Derived from a centroid moment tensor inversion of the long-period surface waves

mwb.name: moment, body wave
mwb.quote: Derived from moment tensor inversion of long-period (~20-200 s; pass band based on size of EQ) body-waves (P- and SH).

mwr.name: moment, regional
mwr.quote: Based on the scalar seismic-moment of the earthquake, derived from moment tensor inversion of the whole seismogram at regional distances

ms.name: surface wave
ms.quote: A magnitude based on the amplitude of Rayleigh surface waves measured at a period near 20 sec.

mb.name: short-period body wave
mb.quote: Based on the amplitude of 1st arriving P-waves at periods of about 1 s.

mfa.name: felt area
mfa.quote: An estimate of body-wave (mb) magnitude based on the size of the area over which the earthquake was felt

ml.name: local
ml.quote: The original magnitude relationship defined by Richter and Gutenberg in 1935 for local earthquakes.

mb_lg.name: short-period surface wave
mb_lg.header: mb_Lg, mb_lg, or MLg (short-period surface wave)
mb_lg.quote: A magnitude for regional earthquakes based on the amplitude of the Lg surface waves as recorded on short-period instruments.

mlg.name: short-period surface wave
mlg.header: mb_Lg, mb_lg, or MLg (short-period surface wave)
mlg.quote: A magnitude for regional earthquakes based on the amplitude of the Lg surface waves as recorded on short-period instruments.

md.name: duration
md.quote: Based on the duration of shaking as measured by the time decay of the amplitude of the seismogram.

mwp.name: integrated P-wave
mwp.quote: Based on an estimate of moment calculated from the integral of the displacement of the P wave recorded on broadband instruments.

mh.name: non-standard method
mh.quote: Non-standard magnitude method. Generally used when standard methods will not work.

mint.name: intensity
mint.quote: A magnitude estimated from the maximum reported intensity, typically for earthquakes occurring before seismic instruments were in general use.

magTypeRule: Labels are matched without regard to case (Md and md, Ml and ml, Mb and mb, Mfa and mfa, Mw and mw). A label the USGS table does not name (for example mc, mlv, mblg) is shown as its code only.
faultAgesNote: No USGS page read for this build states the time bounds of the database’s age classes, so the app prints the class names only.

NORMAL.quote: Volcano is in typical background, noneruptive state or, after a change from a higher level, volcanic activity has ceased and volcano has returned to noneruptive background state.

ADVISORY.quote: Volcano is exhibiting signs of elevated unrest above known background level or, after a change from a higher level, volcanic activity has decreased significantly but continues to be closely monitored for possible renewed increase.

WATCH.quote: Volcano is exhibiting heightened or escalating unrest with increased potential of eruption, timeframe uncertain, OR eruption is underway but poses limited hazards.

WARNING.quote: Hazardous eruption is imminent, underway, or suspected.

GREEN.quote: Volcano is in typical background, non-eruptive state or, after a change from a higher level, volcanic activity has ceased and volcano has returned to noneruptive background state.

YELLOW.quote: Volcano is exhibiting signs of elevated unrest above known background level or, after a change from a higher level, volcanic activity has decreased significantly but continues to be closely monitored for possible renewed increase.

ORANGE.quote: Volcano is exhibiting heightened or escalating unrest with increased potential of eruption, timeframe uncertain, OR eruption is underway with no or minor volcanic-ash emissions [ash- plume height specified, if possible].

RED.quote: Eruption is imminent with significant emission of volcanic ash into the atmosphere likely OR eruption is underway or suspected with significant emission of volcanic ash into the atmosphere [ash-plume height specified, if possible].

eventPageEvidence: USGS’s own record of ci38457511 (the event service’s GeoJSON) gives its url as earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/ci38457511, and that address answered HTTP 200 on 2026-09-30.

software.text: No third-party code ships with this app. The map and its renderer are this app’s own code.
